paras.en: Each day I learnt something about the planet, about the departure, about the journey. It all came little by little, as thoughts happened to arise. That was how, on the third day, I learnt of the drama of the baobabs.
paras.zh: 每天，我都会知道一点关于那颗星球、关于离开、关于旅行的事。这些事随着偶然浮现的思绪，一点一点地显露出来。就这样，到了第三天，我知道了猴面包树带来的灾难。

paras.en: This time, too, it was thanks to the sheep, for the little prince suddenly asked me a question, as though a serious doubt had struck him:
paras.zh: 这一次也还是多亏了那只羊，因为小王子突然问起我来，仿佛心里冒出了一个重大的疑问：

paras.en: “It really is true, isn’t it, that sheep eat shrubs?”
paras.zh: “羊会吃灌木，这是真的，对不对？”

paras.en: I did not understand why it mattered so much that sheep ate shrubs. But the little prince added:
paras.zh: 我不明白，羊会吃灌木这件事为什么那么重要。可小王子又问：

paras.en: I pointed out to the little prince that baobabs are not shrubs, but trees as big as churches, and that even if he took a whole herd of elephants with him, that herd could not finish off a single baobab.
paras.zh: 我向小王子指出，猴面包树不是灌木，而是像教堂一样高大的树，就算他带上整整一群大象，那群大象也对付不了一棵猴面包树。

paras.en: The thought of the herd of elephants made the little prince laugh:
paras.zh: 想到那一群大象，小王子笑了：

paras.en: “You’d have to put them on top of one another...”
paras.zh: “那得把它们一头叠一头地摞起来……”

paras.en: “Baobabs start out small, before they grow big.”
paras.zh: “猴面包树在长大以前，起初也是小小的。”

paras.en: “That’s right! But why do you want your sheep to eat the little baobabs?”
paras.zh: “没错！可你为什么想让你的羊吃小猴面包树呢？”

paras.en: He answered, “Well! Of course!” as though it were obvious. And I had to think very hard to work out this problem all on my own.
paras.zh: 他回答我：“哎！这还用说！”仿佛那是明摆着的事。而我费了好大的脑筋，才独自想明白这个问题。

paras.en: And indeed, on the little prince’s planet, as on all planets, there were good plants and weeds. So there were good seeds from good plants and bad seeds from weeds. But seeds are invisible. They sleep hidden in the earth until one of them feels like waking up. Then it stretches and first sends a lovely, harmless little shoot timidly towards the sun. If it is a radish shoot or a rose bush shoot, you can let it grow as it pleases. But if it is a bad plant, you must pull the plant out at once, as soon as you recognise it. Now there were terrible seeds on the little prince’s planet… they were baobab seeds. The planet’s soil was infested with them. And if you leave it too late to deal with a baobab, you can never get rid of it again. It crowds the whole planet. It pierces it with its roots. And if the planet is too small, and if there are too many baobabs, they make it burst.
paras.zh: 的确，小王子的星球上，和所有星球上一样，有好草，也有坏草。因此，有好草的好种子，也有坏草的坏种子。可是，种子是看不见的。它们睡在泥土的隐秘处，直到其中一颗忽然想要醒来。于是，它伸个懒腰，先怯生生地朝着太阳伸出一根可爱又无害的小嫩枝。如果是萝卜或玫瑰的嫩枝，就可以任它自由生长。但如果是一株坏植物，一认出它来，就得立刻把它拔掉。而小王子的星球上有些可怕的种子……那是猴面包树的种子。星球的土壤里到处都是这些祸害。猴面包树要是动手处理得太晚，就再也没法除掉了。它会挤满整个星球。它用树根把星球穿透。而如果星球太小，如果猴面包树太多，它们就会把星球撑裂。

paras.en: “It’s a matter of discipline,” the little prince told me later. “When you’ve finished your morning wash, you must give the planet a careful wash too. You must make yourself pull out the baobabs regularly, as soon as you can tell them apart from the rose bushes they look so much like when they are very young. It’s very boring work, but very easy.”
paras.zh: “这是个自律的问题，”小王子后来对我说，“早晨给自己洗漱完，就得仔仔细细地给星球也洗漱一番。必须要求自己定时拔掉猴面包树，只要能把它们和玫瑰分辨开，就要动手，它们很小的时候，和玫瑰实在太像了。这活儿很无聊，但很容易。”

paras.en: And one day he advised me to put great care into making a beautiful drawing, so that the children back home would really get this into their heads. “If they travel one day,” he told me, “it could be useful to them. Sometimes there is no harm in putting your work off until later. But with baobabs, it is always a disaster. I knew a planet where a lazy man lived. He had neglected three bushes…”
paras.zh: 有一天，他劝我用心画出一幅好看的画，好让我的家乡的孩子们牢牢记住这件事。“要是他们有一天去旅行，”他对我说，“这也许能派上用场。有时候，把活儿往后拖一拖，并没有什么坏处。可是，如果是猴面包树，拖延就总会酿成灾难。我知道一个星球，上面住着一个懒人。他疏忽了三棵小灌木……”

paras.en: And, following the little prince’s directions, I drew that planet. I do not much like to sound as though I am giving a moral lesson. But so few people know about the danger of baobabs, and the risks for anyone who might lose their way on an asteroid are so great that, just this once, I am setting aside my reserve. I say: “Children! Watch out for baobabs!” I worked so hard on that drawing to warn my friends of a danger they had long been coming close to, just as I had, without knowing it. The lesson I was giving was worth the trouble. You may wonder: Why are there no other drawings in this book as grand as the drawing of the baobabs? The answer is very simple: I tried, but I could not manage it. When I drew the baobabs, I was driven by a sense of urgency.
paras.zh: 于是，我照着小王子的指点，画出了那颗星球。我不大喜欢用说教的口吻讲话。可是，知道猴面包树有多危险的人实在太少，而一个人要是迷失在一颗小行星上，所冒的风险又实在太大，所以，就这一次，我破例不再保持克制。我要说：“孩子们！当心猴面包树！”我的朋友们和我一样，长久以来一直与一种危险擦肩而过，却毫不知情。为了提醒他们，我才在那幅画上下了那么多功夫。我借那幅画传达的这一课，值得我这样费心。你们也许会问：为什么这本书里，没有别的画能像猴面包树那幅画一样壮观呢？答案很简单：我试过，却没能成功。画猴面包树的时候，是一种紧迫感推动着我。
